# Statement formats and presentation notes

Formats follow common US GAAP and IFRS practice. Use the user's own line names and the conventions of the framework they name.

## Income statement (by function)

```text
                         Current  Comparison  Change  Change %  Budget  vs budget
Revenue (by stream)
Total revenue
Cost of revenue
Gross profit
  Gross margin %
Operating expenses (research and development, sales and marketing, general and administrative)
Total operating expenses
Operating income
  Operating margin %
Other income and expense (interest income, interest expense, other)
Income before taxes
Income tax expense
Net income
  Net margin %
```

Notes: classify expenses by function or by nature consistently; if by function, disclose depreciation, amortization and employee benefits by nature in the notes. Show tax as its own line. Discontinued operations are shown separately, net of tax.

## Balance sheet

```text
Current assets: cash and equivalents, short-term investments, receivables (net of allowance), inventory, prepaids
Non-current assets: property and equipment (net), right-of-use assets, goodwill, intangibles (net), long-term investments, other
Total assets
Current liabilities: payables, accrued liabilities, deferred revenue (current), current debt, current lease liabilities
Non-current liabilities: long-term debt, deferred revenue (non-current), lease liabilities, other
Total liabilities
Equity: share capital, additional paid-in capital, retained earnings, other comprehensive income, treasury shares
Total liabilities and equity
```

Current means expected within 12 months or the operating cycle if longer. Goodwill is tested for impairment, not amortized, under US GAAP and IFRS.

## Cash flow statement (indirect method)

```text
Operating: net income; plus non-cash items (depreciation, amortization, share-based pay, deferred tax, gains or losses on disposal, impairment); changes in working capital (receivables, inventory, prepaids, payables, accruals, deferred revenue)
Investing: capital expenditure, purchases and sales of investments, acquisitions net of cash
Financing: debt raised and repaid, shares issued and bought back, dividends
Effect of exchange rates on cash
Net change in cash; opening cash; closing cash
```

Disclose interest and tax paid, and significant non-cash investing and financing activity. Classification of interest and dividends paid can differ between frameworks; follow the user's framework and prior practice.

## Example materiality thresholds (only when the user gives none)

| Line item size | Amount threshold | Percentage threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Large lines | 0.5% of revenue | 5% |
| Medium lines | 0.25% of revenue | 10% |
| Small lines | 0.1% of revenue | 15% |

A variance is material when either threshold is exceeded. Say that these are example thresholds.

## Common period-end adjustments to confirm before drafting

Accruals; deferrals; depreciation and amortization; allowance for credit losses; inventory write-downs; foreign exchange revaluation; tax provision; fair value adjustments; current versus non-current reclassification of debt; intercompany eliminations.
